summary: Feed s149_double is degraded: IDS suffers 9.6% packet loss and 63.9% VXLAN-encapsulated traffic, both blocking complete payload inspection and detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN aggregation is dropping packets under load - 254 of 2644 TCP packets (9.6%, threshold 1%) show gaps indicating buffer exhaustion/oversubscription before the IDS. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is in the visibility fabric, not IDS port overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS TCP reassembly and stream tracking fails with missing segments; signatures that span packets miss, allowing evasion, increasing false negatives and broken flow state for this IDS that needs both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute the feed across multiple IDS ingress ports/broker egress groups to eliminate buffer drops and deliver complete, in-order flows for reliable detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is forwarded from a VXLAN overlay without decapsulation - 1779 of 2782 frames (63.9%, threshold 10%) remain inside VXLAN. Packet broker is passing outer VTEP headers to the tool instead of stripping the tunnel.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers and cannot inspect inner Ethernet/IP payload where attacks reside; with needs_full_payload=true, 63.9% of traffic is blind to signatures, anomaly detection and payload analysis.

recommended_fix.why: Decapsulate/strip VXLAN at the packet broker and forward inner frames to the IDS so it receives the original L2-L7 payload for full signature matching.
